newsitem.title: SPAIN: Copper industry needs greater marketing - Codelco.
newsitem.headline: Copper industry needs greater marketing - Codelco.

text.p: The copper industry must work harder to develop new markets for the metal, given that the next few years could well see oversupply, Marcos Lima Aravena, President and Chief Executive Officer of Chile's CODELCO.

"In the next few years the market may enter an oversupply situation, with production expanding at a rate quite higher than demand. Yet confronted with this prospect, producers have made scant effort to develop the market," he said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.

Unlike other industries, copper has remained focused on production and not directed efforts towards the product. With a few exceptions, price levels in the copper industry have been historically high, Aravena said.
Whereas copper sales in a year would amount to some $20 to $30 billion, promotional activity is costed around $30 to $40 million.
Also unlike other industries and metals the copper industry is not vertically-integrated, which hampers closer knowledge of what is happening downstream.
In aluminium, Alcoa accounts for 13 percent of the total market with 1.9 million tonnes of output, of which 720,000 tonnes is processed into an end-product - cans.
But CODELCO, with 14 percent of Western world production, some 1.2 million tonnes, has nothing as an end-product, he said.
"I believe the time has come to change our outlook - to be more proactive about stimulating potential copper demand," he added.
Aravena called for a new approach among the copper industry to stimulate and promote demand.

"We need to strengthen our efforts with other large copper producers to develop new copper-intensive applications and products and to penetrate new markets with a high potential for consumption," he said.
